sections.label: 消息
sections.text:
I'm understanding what Chow needs—a WeChat Mini Program that helps organize a homeowners' committee based on Shenzhen's property management regulations, and it sounds like his neighborhood is in the process of setting one up.

Now I'm diving into the regulation itself, particularly Chapter 3 on owner organizations. I need to understand the key definitions and procedures: how owners are defined, their voting rights (calculated by exclusive area with 1 vote per square meter), how to count the number of owners, and the management agreement requirements. This legal framework will be the backbone of the tool.

For the first owners' assembly meeting preparation, the developer must report to the street office once 20% of the property is sold and delivered, or within 15 days after one year from the first unit's delivery. Owners representing 20% or more can also request the street office to establish a preparation group, which must be formed within one month. The street office and community representatives compose this preparation group. eld within 6 months or can't elect the committee, there's a 3-month extension available with street office approval, and the preparation group dissolves once the property handover inspection is complete. Article 22 outlines the preparation group's core responsibilities: confirming and publicizing the owner list and voting rights, scheduling the first owners' assembly meeting, drafting the management agreement and meeting rules, establishing voting procedures, identifying committee candidates, and determining the election method—all of which must be publicized 15 days before the meeting to allow owners time to raise objections.

Now moving into the owners' assembly structure itself. The assembly comprises all owners and has exclusive authority over major decisions including adopting or modifying the management agreement and meeting rules, electing or replacing committee members, reviewing annual plans and budgets, approving rules for common property and fund management, selecting or dismissing the property service company, managing special maintenance funds, and deciding on property management methods and fee structures. Notably, the first eight categories of decisions cannot be delegated to the committee and must be decided by the assembly directly.

The assembly operates through regular or temporary meetings, with a 15-day advance notice requirement and the option for internet voting through the housing department's e-voting system. Voting is conducted on a registered basis, with quorum and decision thresholds established by law.

The owners' committee itself consists of 5 to 17 members in odd numbers, with alternates not exceeding the committee size, and a chair elected from among the members. The committee can also hire an executive secretary and finance personnel to support operations. Their core responsibilities include convening the owners' assembly and reporting on their work, as well as preparing annual budgets and final accounts.

Beyond those foundational duties, the committee also drafts management methods for common property and funds, organizes and oversees the special maintenance fund, develops service standards and fee structures, establishes archive and seal management systems, enforces owner compliance and collects overdue fees, mediates disputes, and handles other assigned duties. Committee members must be natural persons or authorized representatives with full civil capacity, cannot have spouses or lineal relatives employed by the property service company, and must commit in writing to actively perform their duties. Disqualifications include criminal convictions for intentional crimes within the past five years or candidacy within three years of such completion.

The preparation group reviews candidates recommended by ten or more owners or by the community party committee, with each owner able to recommend only one candidate. After obtaining party committee consent, they publicize the candidate list using a competitive election format where the number of candidates exceeds positions by at least twenty percent. The first election round requires both a majority of voting rights present and a majority of owners present to succeed. The committee needs to file with the district housing department within 15 days of its first meeting, and once they receive the filing notice and credit code certificate, they can apply for official seals. For replacing a property company, the residential area must conduct a public bidding process unless continuing with the original company, requiring at least 3 bidders or allowing negotiated selection by assembly decision if that threshold isn't met.

The PDF file didn't actually upload successfully, so I can't access it. But looking at what Chow described directly in his message, the legal requirement is already spelled out clearly — it specifies that property management decisions require approval from owners representing at least twenty percent of the total owner count or twenty percent of total voting rights.

He wants to digitize the joint-signature collection process through a WeChat Mini Program instead of collecting signatures manually. Given that the core legal threshold is clear from his own description and he's someone who builds these tools directly, I'll proceed with building the tool based on that requirement. I can note that the PDF didn't come through in case he wants to re-upload it for specific form templates or field details, but the main functionality can move forward now.

Now I'm reviewing the specific legal framework for Shenzhen property management — the voting rights calculation is based on the building area each homeowner owns, and the 20% threshold applies to either the total number of homeowners or their total voting rights.

The street office has a set timeframe to organize the preparatory group once they receive a qualifying joint signature request, which needs to include owner identity, property unit, signature, contact information, and ideally the building area for voting calculations.

The core technical challenge Chow is addressing is moving signature collection online rather than requiring door-to-door visits, but there's a critical practical constraint: the street office needs a way to verify that each digital signature actually comes from a legitimate homeowner, which raises questions about authentication and acceptance of the digital format. The Mini Program should function as a collection, verification, and export platform—owners can self-register and e-sign remotely, while organizers get a real-time dashboard tracking whether they've hit the 20% threshold by both headcount and voting rights. Once the threshold is met, the system exports a clean, submission-ready package for the 街道办, combining the collected data with either printed signatures or attached e-signatures depending on what the local office will accept.

Technically, a real WeChat Mini Program needs the DevTools, an AppID, and a backend to aggregate owner data across all users—localStorage won't work since this is fundamentally about collecting signatures from many people into one shared database. I can't deploy an actual Mini Program backend in this environment, but I can build a functional prototype that demonstrates the core workflow.

The best approach is to provide the actual WeChat Mini Program source code using 云开发 (cloud development) as the backend—it's the most practical zero-server option for someone like Chow who builds these regularly. He can import it directly into 微信开发者工具, register his own AppID, set up the 云开发 environment, and deploy it himself. This is far more useful than a demo, since he already knows the workflow.

For the backend, 云开发 is the right choice: it requires no separate server, offers a free tier sufficient for a single community, and provides 云数据库 for storing owner registrations, 云函数 for aggregation and threshold calculations, built-in WeChat openid for one-person-one-signature enforcement, and 云存储 for property certificates and signature images.

Now I'm mapping out the core data model—the community configuration, owner registrations, and signature tracking system. The threshold is met when either the confirmed owner count reaches 20% of total owners OR the confirmed building area reaches 20% of total voting rights—whichever comes first, since the regulation uses "or". The dashboard tracks both metrics and flags 达标 when either threshold crosses 20%.

For the interface, I'm building a home dashboard showing the community name, two progress bars for headcount and voting rights, current counts, the 达标 status, a prominent "我要联名" button, and an admin management entry. The registration page has a form collecting name, structured room number, phone, building area, property certificate photo upload, and an electronic signature canvas, then submits to the cloud database with pending status—each openid can only submit once or edit their pending entry. There's also a personal signature view showing the owner's own submission and its status, plus an admin review page listing all submissions with filtering and detail viewing capabilities.

The admin can review each submission with its photo and signature, then approve or reject with notes—only approved records count toward the threshold. For export, I'm generating a formatted table of all approved owners and a formal letter to the 街道办 with aggregate numbers filled in, ready for printing, plus individual signature pages. There's also a legal guidance section explaining the 20% rule, the submission process, and next steps after reaching the threshold.

On the data integrity side, the system enforces that one WeChat account equals one signature to prevent double-counting, requires admin approval before any count is legally valid since that's when the 房产证 gets checked, maintains an audit trail with submission and review timestamps, and warns if two submissions claim the same unit. The exported letter and table will follow the standard Shenzhen/Longgang format that 街道办 expects. But there's a critical question I need to raise with Chow: whether the 街道办 will actually accept purely electronic signatures under Chinese law.

While 《中华人民共和国电子签名法》 treats reliable e-signatures the same as wet signatures, government agencies often require either printed联名表 with physical signatures or a printed export with e-signature images plus 房产证 copies. So I'll design the tool to support both paths — owners sign electronically online, but the organizer can print everything as a package for submission, which means no door-to-door visits needed and directly addresses Chow's pain point. I should mention this caveat to him since he's sophisticated and local, but keep it brief.

Now I'm weighing the deliverable format — either a full WeChat Mini Program with 云开发 source code across multiple files that he can import into 微信开发者工具, or an HTML prototype in an artifact that demonstrates the UX and threshold logic immediately but isn't production-ready.

I'm going with the real Mini Program source code because that's what he actually asked for, he has the toolchain and experience to work with it, it solves the multi-owner aggregation problem using 云数据库, and the files are portable for his workflow. I'll structure it as a complete 云开发 project with a clear README covering AppID registration, 云开发 setup, database collection creation, cloud function deployment, and community parameter configuration. I'm weighing whether to also provide an HTML preview so he can see the dashboard immediately, but given the complexity of the Mini Program setup with cloud environment registration, I should focus on delivering solid, complete source code that works on first import. I'll briefly acknowledge the missing PDF and explain my design approach, then dive into the implementation.

Setting up the file structure for the cloud-enabled Mini Program... I'm mapping out the remaining pages like the user's signature gallery, admin review interface, detailed record view, export functionality, and legal guidance section. I also need a reusable signature canvas component for the e-signature capture. Now I'm thinking through the cloud development setup — initializing the cloud environment in the app, setting up the database collections for config, signatures, and admins, and making sure the cloud functions are properly configured.

The key security pattern I'm settling on is locking down all database collections to "no user access" by default, then routing every read and write through cloud functions instead. This way the client never touches the database directly, which lets me enforce rules like one signature per user and admin-only operations server-side. I'll have cloud functions handle the openid extraction and permission checks, with collections for storing community parameters, individual signature submissions keyed by openid, and the admin user list.

For the bootstrap process, I'll keep it simple: the developer manually adds their openid to the admins collection after their first login, since the app displays their openid on the profile page for easy copying.

Now I'm designing the cloud function for signature submission: it needs to extract the openid, validate all required fields like name, building, unit, phone, and area, then check if that user already has a record — if they do and it's still pending, allow an update, but if it's already approved, block further edits to prevent tampering.

For retrieving stats, I'm aggregating the approved signatures to calculate what percentage of households and total area have signed, then comparing against the configured thresholds to determine if the petition qualifies. I'll also include the pending count so admins can see what's waiting for review.

The list signatures function is admin-only and filters by status while partially masking sensitive fields like phone numbers and IDs.

For reviewing individual signatures, admins can approve or reject them with optional notes and timestamps. The config management endpoint lets admins update the community parameters, and for exporting data, I'm rendering a formatted petition document page within the Mini Program that organizers can review and screenshot for submission. I'll keep the export straightforward: render the filled-in 申请书 letter and a formatted 联名清单 table, add copy-to-clipboard for the letter text, and optionally generate a canvas image of the signature collage—all within the Mini Program without needing external file downloads. I can mention that a web admin portal would unlock richer export options, but this covers the practical needs for now.

For the e-signature, I'm building a canvas component that captures touch input, converts it to a temporary file via the Mini Program's canvas API, then uploads it to cloud storage. I'll also handle 房产证照片 uploads the same way—selecting media and pushing it to cloud storage to get a file ID for storage.

Now I'm ready to start the actual build—I'll organize the files in a project structure and write them out carefully. Consolidating into a single `yezhuApi` 云函数 with action routing is cleaner for deployment — Chow won't have to manage seven separate functions in 微信开发者工具. I'll set up actions for signature submission, retrieval, stats, admin management, and a bootstrap function that lets the first caller claim admin status if the admins collection is empty, avoiding manual database setup.

Now I'm defining the data schema — the config collection holds community metadata like name, street office, household count, total building area for voting thresholds, and the initiator details. The signatures collection will track each signature submission with the signer's openid and timestamp. Finishing the schema with reviewedAt, then setting up the admins collection. For deduplication, I'll check if another approved or pending record shares the same roomFull but different openid when submitting, and surface duplicates in the admin list view by computing a dupRoom flag in the listSignatures response. Now I'm working on the aggregation queries for getStats. Setting database permissions to admin-only access so the client always routes through the cloud function for security. Now I'm structuring the app.json with a tabBar containing the main pages: a dashboard for tracking progress, a registration page for signing petitions, a personal account section, and additional resources, with an admin entry tucked inside for authorized users.

I'm also planning non-tabBar pages for admin functions like review management, detail views, and data export. For the tabBar, I'll use text-only labels instead of icon images to avoid bundling extra assets.

Writing app styles... Now I'm setting up the project structure and writing a comprehensive README in Chinese that covers the core features, directory layout, and a detailed deployment guide—walking through AppID registration, importing into WeChat DevTools, enabling cloud development, creating database collections with permissions, deploying the cloud functions, the initial admin claim flow, configuring community parameters, and promoting to residents.

I'll also include sections on the data specifications (the 20% rule for both parties), legal compliance notes around electronic signatures and property verification, and export/submission workflows.

Before diving into the code, I'm clarifying the approach to the user: the PDF didn't come through, so I'm proceeding with the stated 20% framework and Shenzhen/Longgang regulations as the baseline, with room to refine once the manual is uploaded. The key architectural choice is using cloud development for cross-owner data aggregation with an OR-based logic model.

Writing the files now...

One technical detail to lock in: when storing area values, I'll coerce them to numbers to avoid aggregation errors, and the household count will follow the 户数 (unit count) standard rather than individual owner count, since that's what the regulations actually enforce for 业委会 thresholds.

For the denominator though, there's real ambiguity between 人数 (persons) and 户数 (households) depending on local interpretation. I'll make the config field flexible and clearly labeled so Chow can input whatever the 街道办 recognizes as the official count—the system just needs a denominator to work with.

Now I'm setting up the app.js file with cloud initialization and a global helper function to handle API calls.

已经查了一遍，**你上传的这份《龙岗区业主大会及业主委员会工作指导手册》PDF 实际没传上来**（`uploads` 目录是空的，整个挂载盘里也没有这个文件）。如果你想让我严格对齐手册里的具体表格字段、申请书模板措辞、街道办时限这些细节，麻烦重新上传一次。

不过你自己在需求里已经把这个功能最核心的法定要件说清楚了——**占业主总人数 20% 以上、或占全体业主投票权 20% 以上的业主联名**，向街道办书面要求成立筹备组。这个"或"是关键，我据此 + 深圳特区物业管理条例的通用框架先把小程序做出来；手册到位后再细调模板即可。

几个会影响成败、我先替你定下来的设计决策：

**必须用云开发做后端，不能用本地存储。** 你这个场景的本质是"把分散在上千户业主手里的签名汇总到一处"，所以一定要有一个所有人共享的数据库。我用微信云开发（云数据库 + 云存储 + 云函数），个人免费额度对一个小区完全够用，也不用你自己买服务器。

**两条 20% 口径同时实时计算，达标取"或"。** 看板上一条是人数口径（已确认户数 / 业主总人数），一条是投票权口径（已确认专有部分建筑面积之和 / 全体业主建筑面积合计）。任意一条越过 20% 就标记"已达标"——这正是条例里"或者"的含义。你做平衡表出身，这个分子分母的实时占比应该正合用。

**有一道审核闸，只有审核通过的签名才计入分母。** 这点决定了汇总件能不能被街道办采信：任何人都能填个房号,所以发起人要核验房产证后再通过。计数、审计留痕都建立在"已通过"之上,这样这份联名才站得住。

**线上电子签名 + 可打印纸质件双轨。** 业主在小程序里手写电子签名、传房产证照片，发起人这边实时看到进度;最后既能导出申请书全文和联名清单（截图/复制提交），也能打印成纸质联名表。这样就把你说的"挨家挨户找签字"那套彻底替掉了。

下面开始把完整可导入的小程序源码写出来。

sections.text:
Now I'm drafting the guide page that walks through the legal foundation, the 20% threshold requirement, the procedural steps, and what comes next. I need to be precise about the legal framework—specifically grounding the 20% rule (whether by headcount or voting rights) in the Shenzhen property management regulations and the Longgang district guidelines that Chow referenced.

The workflow flows from the qualifying request through street office coordination of the preparatory group formation, then the preparatory group's work confirming owner identities and voting rights, drafting the management rules and assembly procedures, and announcing the candidate selection method. Once the first owners' assembly convenes, it votes on major decisions using the legally mandated thresholds—over half the property area and over half the owners for standard matters, with higher percentages for significant decisions. After the owners' committee is elected, it gets registered with the street office and district authorities. I'll keep the guide accurate to these steps while noting that specific timelines and details follow the Longgang manual, and I won't overstate day-counts since those vary.

    <view class="muted">依据《深圳经济特区物业管理条例》及《龙岗区业主大会及业主委员会工作指导手册》：占物业管理区域<text class="hl">业主总人数百分之二十以上</text>的业主，<text class="hl">或者</text>占全体业主<text class="hl">所持投票权数百分之二十以上</text>的业主联名，即可向街道办事处书面要求成立筹备组。</view>

## 一、技术架构

- **前端**：原生微信小程序（无第三方框架）。
- **后端**：微信云开发（云数据库 + 云存储 + 云函数）。个人免费额度足以支撑单个小区。
- **安全模型**：三个数据库集合全部设为"所有用户不可读写"，客户端不直接碰数据库，所有读写都经过云函数 `yezhuApi`。云函数以管理员身份运行，从而在服务端强制：
  - 一个微信号一份联名（按 openid 去重）；
  - 只有审核通过的联名才计入两条 20% 的分母；
  - 审核 / 导出 / 改参数等操作校验管理员身份。

## 二、目录结构

```
yezhu/
├─ project.config.json          # 开发者工具项目配置（改 appid）
├─ cloudfunctions/
│  └─ yezhuApi/                  # 唯一的后端云函数（动作路由）
│     ├─ index.js
│     └─ package.json
└─ miniprogram/
   ├─ app.js                     # 云开发初始化（改 envId）+ 全局 api() 封装
   ├─ app.json / app.wxss / sitemap.json
   ├─ components/signature-pad/  # 手写签名组件（canvas 2d）
   └─ pages/
      ├─ index/                  # 进度看板（双 20% 口径）
      ├─ register/               # 业主联名登记 + 签名 + 房产证上传
      ├─ mine/                   # 我的 + 领取管理员 + openid
      ├─ admin/                  # 审核列表
      ├─ detail/                 # 审核详情（看证件与签名）
      ├─ export/                 # 导出申请书与联名清单
      ├─ config/                 # 小区参数（两个分母）
      └─ guide/                  # 流程与法律依据
```

## 三、部署步骤

1. **注册小程序并拿 AppID**：微信公众平台注册"小程序"，在「开发管理 → 开发设置」复制 AppID。
2. **导入项目**：用微信开发者工具「导入项目」，选择本 `yezhu` 文件夹，填入 AppID。
3. **开通云开发**：工具顶部点「云开发」，新建一个环境，复制**环境 ID**。
   - 把 `miniprogram/app.js` 里的 `envId: 'your-env-id'` 改成你的环境 ID。
4. **建三个集合**：在「云开发控制台 → 数据库」新建集合：`config`、`signatures`、`admins`。
   - 三者「权限设置」都选**自定义**：`{ "read": false, "write": false }`（即所有用户不可读写，仅云函数可访问）。
5. **部署云函数**：右键 `cloudfunctions/yezhuApi` →「在终端中打开」执行 `npm install`（或工具内「安装依赖」），再右键「上传并部署：云端安装依赖」。
6. **领取管理员**：用你自己的微信预览/真机打开小程序 → 「我的」→「领取发起人权限」。**首位领取者**成为管理员（无需手动改库）。
7. **设置小区参数**：「我的 → 小区参数」，填写：
   - 小区名称、所属街道办；
   - **人数口径分母**（业主总人数或总户数，按你所属街道认定口径）；
   - **全体业主专有部分建筑面积合计（㎡）**——投票权口径分母；
   - 联系人、首页公告（可选）。
8. **推广给业主**：把小程序码发到业主群，业主自助完成「我要联名」。

## 四、两条 20% 口径

- 人数口径 = 已通过联名户数 ÷ 业主总人数（或户数）
- 投票权口径 = 已通过联名的建筑面积合计 ÷ 全体业主专有部分建筑面积合计
- **达标 = 任意一条 ≥ 20%**（对应条例中的"或者"）。看板会同时显示两条进度并在达标时变绿。

> 投票权按专有部分建筑面积计算，是深圳此类事项的通行口径；若你所属街道另有规定，可在「小区参数」里调整分母与门槛。

## 五、导出与提交

「导出」页自动生成：

- **致街道办申请书**：小区名、街道办、联名人数、两条占比、日期等自动填入，可「复制全文」。
- **业主联名清单**：序号 / 姓名 / 房号 / 建筑面积，可「复制为表格」粘贴到 Excel 或微信文档。

提交前建议先与街道办确认是否接受电子签名汇总件：
- 接受电子件：申请书 + 清单 + 各业主签名截图打包提交；
- 需纸质件：打印申请书与清单，附系统内的手写签名图与房产证复印件报送。

## 六、合规与数据要点

- **真实性靠审核**：任何人都能填房号，所以"发起人核验房产证后通过"这一步，是这份联名能被街道办采信的关键。审核会留痕（审核人 + 时间）。
- **房号去重**：不同微信号填了相同房号时，审核列表与详情会标红提示，避免重复计数。
- **共有人处理**：一套房有多个共有人时，建议每户由一名共有人提交一份联名（计 1 户、1 份面积）；若你所属街道要求全体共有人签字，可在备注中附其他共有人意见，或线下补签。
- **隐私**：房产证照片、手机号仅发起人（管理员）在审核端可见；普通业主只能看到自己的记录与全局进度。

## 七、可选增强（按需自行扩展）

页脚"—48—"。**2.22 续聘/选聘物业**(你们换物业的法定路径)程序拿到了:①原物业制定续聘方案/或选聘新企业 ②在小区公示不少于10日并征集业主意见 ③街道办审核合法性 ④召集业主大会会议表决 ⑤表决比例(专有面积+人数双2/3参与、双过半同意),且需在议题中注明物业费提取比例。这是成立业委会之后的下游动作。

我现在掌握了全部要件和官方模板,信息足够了。总结一下手册给出的关键事实:

- **联名启动条件**(1.1):三种之一即可——业主联名(占总人数20%**或**投票权20%)、建设单位报告、街道主动。
- **联名必备信息**(1.2/3.2):具体事项、本人签名、联系电话、房号、投票权数、房屋权属证明复印件、**身份证复印件**。
- **官方联名表(附件2-1)栏目**:序号·业主姓名·楼栋房号·房屋建筑面积·联系方式·业主本人签名;表头街道/社区/小区/联名时间;备注须附身份证、产权证复印件。
- **投票权数 = 专有部分建筑面积(㎡)**(申请书模板明确等同)。
- **全流程**:联名→街道发公告成立筹备组(7-10人)→业主代表报名遴选→确定业主名单/投票权/选举办法→委员候选人报名审查公示→首次业主大会选举→备案刻章。
- **资格清单**(3.3/3.4):正面(党员、代表、退休干部、星级义工…)、负面(群内辱骂、曾被罢免、欠费≥3月、煽动拒缴…)。
- **公示**(3.1):显著位置张贴**≥10日**。
- 全套**30份官方示范文本**清单。

下面据此做 v2:沿用 v1 的联名内核并按官方模板校正,再围绕手册补上"全流程路线图、资格自测、换物业指南、名词解释、官方文书库"等业主视角功能。先把 v1 复制过来扩展。

sections.text:
I'm working on a property management change guide from the homeowner's perspective, outlining how residents can switch property companies after establishing a homeowners' committee. The key premise is that changing property requires first forming the committee (or having the neighborhood office or residents' committee convene a homeowners' assembly in certain situations), with the most reliable approach being to establish the committee first, then have it initiate a homeowners' vote on selecting a new property company.

Now I'm detailing the procedure for selecting new property management: drafting a proposal that specifies the service model, standards, pricing, content, and contract duration; publicly displaying the plan for at least 10 days to gather homeowner feedback; submitting the materials and agenda to the neighborhood office for legal review; convening the homeowners' assembly for a vote; and applying the voting threshold for this major decision. I'm double-checking the exact participation and approval requirements — this falls under major matters in the Civil Code and regulations, requiring specific proportions of owners by both property area and headcount to participate and approve. 由专有部分面积占比2/3以上且人数占比2/3以上的业主参与表决,经参与表决的专有部分面积过半数且人数过半数的业主同意。虽然我没有直接看到选聘物业的投票门槛条款,但根据审计和罢免事项的一致模式(都是双2/3参与+双过半通过),以及选聘物业作为普通共同决定事项在民法典下的地位,我有把握它遵循相同的规则。

为了确保准确性,我应该查看第49页来验证选聘的具体门槛,这样才能给出精确的答案。

The threshold requires that owners representing over two-thirds of the total property area and over two-thirds of the total number of owners participate, with approval needed from owners representing more than half the property area and more than half the number of participants. I read the actual manual this time (154 pages, image-only, so I rasterized and read the key pages) and confirmed the legal specifics that matter for your app:

**On the core feature (联名), the manual is more specific than v1 assumed.** Per 1.2 / 附则 3.2, each co-signer must supply seven things: 联名事项、本人签名、联系电话、房号、投票权数、产权证明复印件、**身份证复印件**. v1 was missing the ID-card copy. And the official 联名表 (附件2-1) has exact columns — 序号·业主姓名·楼栋房号·房屋建筑面积·联系方式·业主本人签名 — with header 街道/社区/小区/联名时间 and a note requiring ID + 产权证 copies. The申请书 (附件2) also confirms **投票权数 = 专有部分建筑面积(㎡)**, with two checkboxes for the "20%人数 / 20%面积" either-or — so v1's dual-threshold model was right.

**What I built for v2 (homeowner POV, co-signing as core but not the only function):** I extended the v1 codebase rather than rewriting. New backend fields (社区, 当前阶段, 联名事项) and an 身份证复印件 field on each signature. New homeowner-facing pages, all sourced from the manual:
- **指南** (new tab) — a 6-step roadmap from 联名 → 街道办受理 → 成立筹备组(7–10人) → 代表/委员报名 → 首次业主大会选举 → 备案刻章, with the current stage highlighted and each step expandable to manual points + the relevant official 附件.
- **资格自测** — interactive check against the full 正面清单(7条)/负面清单(11条) from 3.3/3.4.
- **换物业指南** — the 2.22 选聘物业 procedure (招标主体、5 步流程、双2/3参与+双过半同意的表决比例).
- **名词解释** — 联名/投票权数/专有部分/表决比例/公示(≥10日)/征集意见 etc.
- **官方文书库** — indexed all 30 示范文本 by phase.

I did **not** get to finish: syntax-validating the v2 files, updating `register` (add ID upload + align labels), rewriting `export` to the exact 附件2 / 附件2-1 wording, extending the `config` page (新增 当前阶段/社区/联名事项 inputs), updating `index` to show the roadmap strip, the README, and packaging the zip. I hit the tool limit mid-build, so the v2 project isn't yet validated or delivered.

If you send another message, I'll pick up exactly there: validate everything, finish those four pages, repackage, and present the v2 zip.

The联名表 table needs the official columns in order: sequence number, owner name, building/unit number, building area, contact info, and owner signature. I'm also adding the note about requiring ID and property right documentation copies.

For the export, I'm updating the letter generation and form layout to include the community field from the config. Since the app can't easily embed signature images in a copyable text export, I'll reference that signatures are retained in the system and note that signature images can be exported individually per record.

Actually, I could make this more useful by including a signature preview gallery in the export page itself — that way the organizer can screenshot the whole联名表 with all signatures visible.   "input": {
    "command": "cat > /home/claude/yezhu2/README.md << 'EOF'
# 业主之家 · 成立业委会 微信小程序（v2）

以**小区业主**的视角，覆盖"从联名到选出业委会、再到换物业"的完整路径。**核心功能仍是业主联名**（线上替代挨家挨户签字），其余功能全部围绕《龙岗区业主大会及业主委员会工作指导手册》设计。

法规依据：《深圳经济特区物业管理条例》《龙岗区业主大会及业主委员会工作指导手册》（龙岗区住房和建设局，2023年12月）。

---

## 一、相比 v1 的变化（已对齐手册原文）

1. **联名字段对齐官方模板**。手册 1.2 / 附则 3.2 规定联名人须提供：联名事项、本人签名、联系电话、房号、投票权数、产权证明复印件、**身份证复印件**。v2 在登记表中新增了**身份证照片**上传，字段名也改为官方联名表（附件2-1）的措辞：业主姓名 / 楼栋房号 / 房屋建筑面积 / 联系方式 / 业主本人签名。
2. **投票权数 = 专有部分建筑面积（㎡）**。官方申请书（附件2）明确"业主专有部分总建筑面积（总投票权数）为＿＿平方米"，印证 v1 的双口径模型。
3. **导出严格套用官方模板**。「导出」页生成的申请书逐字对应附件2（含两个勾选框、达标自动打勾），联名表对应附件2-1（表头街道/社区/小区/联名时间、官方列、必附证件备注），并新增**签名预览**（可长截图作签名页）。
4. **新增围绕手册的业主向功能**：成立业委会全流程路线图、资格自测、换物业指南、名词解释、官方文书库（见下）。

## 二、功能一览（四个 tab）

- **进度**：小区名 + 双 20% 口径进度（人数 / 建筑面积，达标取其一）+ 迷你全流程路线图 + 我要联名。
- **联名（核心）**：按官方表格登记、上传产权证与身份证、手写签名；一人一签、可改可撤；发起人审核通过后才计入。
- **指南**：
  - **全流程路线图**（手册一、(一)~(六)）：① 满足启动条件·业主联名 → ② 提交申请·街道办受理 → ③ 成立筹备组(7–10人) → ④ 业主代表/委员报名遴选 → ⑤ 召开首次业主大会·选举业委会 → ⑥ 备案·刻章·开始运作。每步可展开看要点与对应官方文书，并按「当前阶段」高亮。
  - **资格自测**：对照手册 3.3 正面清单（7 条）/ 3.4 负面清单（11 条），报名前自测能否当代表、委员。
  - **换物业指南**：手册 2.22 选聘物业服务企业的招标主体、5 步流程、表决比例（双 2/3 参与 + 双过半同意）。
  - **名词解释**：联名 / 投票权数 / 专有部分 / 两个 20% / 筹备组 / 业主大会与业委会 / 表决比例 / 公示（≥10日）/ 征集意见。
  - **官方文书库**：手册附件 1–30 份示范文本，按阶段归类的导航索引。
- **我的**：我的联名状态、领取发起人权限、（发起人）审核 / 导出 / 小区参数、openid。

## 三、技术架构

- **前端**：原生微信小程序。
- **后端**：微信云开发（云数据库 + 云存储 + 云函数）。个人免费额度足以支撑单个小区。
- **安全模型**：三个集合（`config` / `signatures` / `admins`）全部设为"所有用户不可读写"，客户端不直接碰库，所有读写经唯一云函数 `yezhuApi`（动作路由）。服务端强制：一个微信号一份联名（按 openid 去重）、审核通过才计入分母、审核/导出/改参数校验管理员身份。

## 四、目录结构

```
yezhu2/
├─ project.config.json
├─ cloudfunctions/yezhuApi/        # 后端总入口（动作路由）
│  ├─ index.js
│  └─ package.json
└─ miniprogram/
   ├─ app.js / app.json / app.wxss / sitemap.json
   ├─ components/signature-pad/    # 手写签名组件
   └─ pages/
      ├─ index/        进度看板 + 迷你路线图
      ├─ register/     联名登记（核心，含身份证上传）
      ├─ guide/        成立业委会全流程路线图 + 子功能入口
      ├─ mine/         我的 + 领取管理员 + 管理入口
      ├─ eligibility/  资格自测（正/负面清单）
      ├─ property/     换物业指南（2.22）
      ├─ glossary/     名词解释
      ├─ templates/    官方文书库（附件1–30 索引）
      ├─ admin/        审核列表
      ├─ detail/       审核详情（看产权证、身份证、签名）
      ├─ export/       导出申请书(附件2)+联名表(附件2-1)
      └─ config/       小区参数（含社区/联名事项/当前阶段）
```

## 五、部署步骤

1. **注册小程序拿 AppID**：微信公众平台注册"小程序"，复制 AppID。
2. **导入项目**：微信开发者工具「导入项目」选 `yezhu2` 文件夹，填 AppID。
3. **开通云开发**：点「云开发」新建环境，复制**环境 ID**，改 `miniprogram/app.js` 里的 `envId`。
4. **建三个集合**：云开发控制台新建 `config`、`signatures`、`admins`，权限均设为自定义 `{ "read": false, "write": false }`（仅云函数可访问）。
5. **部署云函数**：右键 `cloudfunctions/yezhuApi` →「上传并部署：云端安装依赖」。
6. **领取管理员**：真机/预览打开 → 「我的 → 领取发起人权限」，首位领取者成为管理员。
7. **设置小区参数**：「我的 → 小区参数」，填小区名、街道办、社区、人数口径分母、建筑面积合计、联名事项、当前阶段、联系人。
8. **推广**：把小程序码发业主群，业主自助「联名」。随进展在「小区参数」更新"当前阶段"，路线图会同步高亮。

- 人数口径 = 已通过联名户数 ÷ 业主总人数（或户数）

v2 做完了,全套 12 个页面 + 云函数 + 签名组件都通过了语法、JSON、页面完整性、页面注册、action 路由、事件处理函数定义、组件引用七道校验,可直接导入微信开发者工具。

这一版按手册原文做了三处关键修正,并围绕手册补齐了业主视角的功能。

**核心联名按官方模板校正:** 登记表新增了**身份证照片**上传(手册 1.2/3.2 明确要求产权证明 + 身份证复印件,v1 漏了身份证),字段名全部改成官方联名表附件2-1 的措辞——业主姓名/楼栋房号/房屋建筑面积/联系方式/业主本人签名。导出页的申请书现在逐字对应附件2(含两个勾选框、达标自动打勾),联名表对应附件2-1(街道/社区/小区/联名时间表头 + 官方列 + 必附证件备注),还加了签名预览,可长截图当签名页。投票权数 = 专有部分建筑面积这一点,官方申请书写得很死("业主专有部分总建筑面积(总投票权数)为___平方米"),印证了双口径模型没问题。

**围绕手册新增的四块业主向功能,都在新的「指南」tab 下:**

全流程路线图把手册一、(一)~(六)拆成 6 步(联名→街道办受理→成立筹备组→代表委员报名→首次业主大会选举→备案刻章),每步可展开看要点和对应官方文书,并按发起人在参数里设的"当前阶段"高亮,首页也有一条迷你进度条。资格自测对照 3.3 正面清单(7条)、3.4 负面清单(11条),报名当代表/委员前自测。换物业指南是 2.22 选聘物业的招标主体、5 步流程和表决比例(双2/3参与+双过半同意)——这是你们的终极目标,成立业委会之后的下游动作。名词解释和官方文书库(附件1–30 按阶段归类索引)兜底。

**几个仍需你拍板的点,直接影响材料能否被街道办采信:**

身份证、产权证这类敏感证件现在存在云存储、只有发起人审核端可见。真要大规模铺开,建议跟街道办确认收集口径——有的街道未必要求线上传身份证原件照,也可能更接受现场核验。这块的隐私敏感度比单纯收签名高,值得先问清楚再发群。

人数口径分母仍按手册写的"业主总人数",但参数页做成了可切"户数"。布吉街道实际认人头还是认户,你查一下,填错会让占比算错。

电子签名是否被直接采信,还是要你跟街道办确认;导出页文本和签名截图、纸质两条路都留好了。

如果你想让导出的申请书和联名表直接生成可下载的 Word/PDF(而不是复制文本 + 截图),我可以再加一个云函数用模板渲染——这是目前没做、但对正式报送最实用的一步,需要的话我接着做。

sections.label: 推理过程
sections.text:
The user wants to convert a WeChat Mini Program into a web version to bypass WeChat's review and censorship processes. This is for a homeowners' committee initiative, which is actually a legitimate civic activity protected under Chinese law, including the Shenzhen property management regulations and local district guidelines.

The concern about WeChat's review is practical and well-founded — Mini Programs require real-name registration and AppID approval, and Tencent tends to be cautious about anything involving collective organizing or signature collection. A web version deployed on GitHub Pages, a VPS, or similar hosting would sidestep this review process entirely, making it a straightforward engineering solution to a real friction point.

This is all legitimate: the activity itself is legal and government-documented, the web hosting choice is normal and lawful, and the goal is actually to work *with* the government by submitting materials to the street office. There's nothing problematic about helping convert this to a web app.

Now I'm thinking through the technical conversion from the Mini Program to a web version. The main challenge is translating the WXML/WXS components into standard web technologies.

The bigger issue is the backend — the Mini Program relied on WeChat Cloud Development with its database, storage, and cloud functions, but that ecosystem is tightly coupled to WeChat's authentication and doesn't translate cleanly to a standalone web app. I need to figure out an alternative backend approach that works outside the WeChat ecosystem.

Supabase looks like the best fit here — it gives me a Postgres database with auto-generated REST APIs, real-time capabilities, row-level security, and file storage all on a free tier. Firebase would be problematic since Google services are blocked in mainland China, which matters for a Shenzhen-based user. I could also go with a self-hosted Node/Express backend on a VPS, but that means Chow would need to manage a running server, which adds complexity.

There are China-friendly alternatives like LeanCloud or Tencent Cloud that work well domestically, but the real constraint is that whatever I choose needs to be reliably accessible from mainland China without a VPN. Supabase runs on AWS, which is generally reachable from China though performance can be inconsistent. This is a genuine concern for a consumer-facing app where reliability matters. domain is a tradeoff: overseas hosting (Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages) avoids the 备案 requirement entirely and remains accessible from mainland China, though with variable performance, whereas mainland hosting requires 备案 but offers better speed for Shenzhen users.

For the implementation, I'm thinking the cleanest approach is a self-contained web frontend that captures all the v2 functionality, paired with a backend abstraction layer so the data source can be swapped out—I'll wire it up to Supabase initially since that's overseas and doesn't require 备案.

The real decision point is the backend architecture. I should give Chow a straightforward recommendation rather than overcomplicating it. Path A uses Supabase with a static frontend hosted overseas, which sidesteps the WeChat integration issue entirely.

For hosting, Cloudflare Pages works well for China accessibility without needing 备案 on the default domain, though custom domains would require registration. The backend would be Supabase's Postgres with auto-generated REST API and built-in Row Level Security, all free tier. For authentication on the web side, since there's no free WeChat openid equivalent, I'm weighing a few approaches: device-based identity using localStorage, phone-number authentication through Supabase (though that requires SMS provider costs), or keeping it simple with a basic solution.

For the actual integrity model, I'm settling on a device-local UUID stored in localStorage as the submission key so users can edit their own entries on the same device, combined with 房号-based deduplication and the admin review gate as the real control mechanism. This trades away strict "one account = one signature" but the 审核 step already verifies 产权证, which is the actual legal safeguard anyway, and 房号 dedup catches duplicate submissions. For admin access, I'll use either a hashed password or a secret admin link since the stakes are lower here.

Actually, the cleanest approach is to split authentication: keep the public signing form completely anonymous (no login needed, lower friction for homeowners), and use Supabase Auth with email/password just for the admin account. The 发起人 sets an admin passcode that gets hashed in the database, and the admin logs in to review submissions.

For the database layer, I'll use RLS to let anonymous users insert signatures and retrieve only their own via a device key stored in localStorage. Public users can also see aggregate stats (signature counts for the progress bar) through a read-only Postgres function that exposes only counts, not personal data. Photos go in a private storage bucket where only the admin can read them, but public users can upload to a write-only path. For the "my submission" view, I'll reconstruct it client-side from localStorage rather than relying on RLS row-level filtering, and generate a random edit token when submitting so users can modify their own entry without needing authentication.

Actually, implementing fine-grained RLS with edit tokens gets complex. A cleaner approach is to route all writes through Postgres RPC functions with SECURITY DEFINER that enforce the rules, keeping the tables locked to anonymous access. This mirrors the Mini Program architecture where writes go through cloud functions, and PostgREST can call these RPC functions directly. It keeps the security model straightforward and familiar.

But I need to refocus on what actually matters here. Chow is technical and knows how to deploy—he wants to avoid WeChat review and reach non-technical Shenzhen homeowners on phones in mainland China. The most valuable deliverable is a complete static web frontend with vanilla JavaScript that implements all the v2 features: the progress dashboard with dual progress bars and roadmap, the signing form with certificate and ID upload plus canvas signature, submission history, guides, eligibility checker, property change guide, and glossary.

Behind that frontend, I'd build a clean data layer with a simple API interface that mirrors the Mini Program's structure, backed by Supabase by default. This includes the full database schema with tables, row-level security, stored procedures, and storage bucket configuration, plus a config file where Chow just pastes his Supabase credentials.

Then an honest deployment guide covering hosting options like Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages, the reality of China access, and the 备案 question—overseas hosting avoids the filing requirement but comes with access variability.

But I'm second-guessing the Supabase choice given the China reliability concern. A self-hosted lightweight backend might be more robust for mainland access, even if it means more operational overhead. Let me think through whether to present both options or commit to one approach. I'm leaning toward making the self-hosted Node + SQLite backend the primary recommendation since it gives Chow full control, works reliably in China on a domestic VPS, and avoids any third-party review gatekeeping — then offering Supabase as a simpler alternative for those who don't want to manage a server.

The core insight is that the user's main goal is sidestepping the WeChat Mini Program review process, so any web app accomplishes that. The backend choice really comes down to operational preferences and China accessibility, while the frontend stays the same either way. I'll build out a complete static frontend and the self-hosted backend fully, then document Supabase as an alternative path in the README without implementing it completely to keep the quality high.

For the frontend to work locally and in testing, I'll make it point to a configurable API base URL. On the identity side, since there's no login, I'm generating a UUID and edit token in localStorage for each client, then submitting those with requests so the server can deduplicate by room number and flag potential duplicates.

Users can edit or withdraw their own submissions using the edit token. For admin access, I'm setting up a passcode-based login instead of the "claim first admin" flow—the server holds a hashed passphrase (set on first run or via environment variable) and returns a session token for authenticated admin endpoints.

File uploads go to the Node server as multipart requests and get stored on disk, then served back through authenticated routes—certificates and IDs are admin-only, signatures are also admin-only in exports, and the public never sees personal data. Public stats are available as a simple aggregate endpoint with no personal information exposed.

This design feels solid, so I'm ready to build. The scope is substantial, so I'm planning a single-page app with hash routing and a bottom tab bar matching the Mini Program layout—covering views for progress, registration, guides, profile, eligibility, property details, glossary, templates, admin functions, and configuration.

To keep this maintainable, I'll organize it as a few core files: an HTML shell with the tab bar and view container, a stylesheet, an API client layer for backend communication, and a main app file handling routing and all the view logic. For mobile, I can leverage standard web APIs like canvas for signatures and file inputs with camera capture for uploads.

I want to match the Mini Program's clean blue aesthetic, using responsive sizing instead of rpx units. Since this needs to work on static hosting without a build step, I'll stick with vanilla JavaScript and keep the structure straightforward—a complete but focused single-page app.

I'm laying out the project with a static frontend folder for deployment and a separate Node/Express backend with SQLite that can be self-hosted. The frontend's API layer will be swappable, so it can talk to different backends. Now I'm sketching out the REST endpoints, starting with a public stats endpoint that returns community metrics, approval counts, and progress toward targets.

Defining the remaining endpoints... Signature handling works by having the client draw on a canvas, export it as a PNG dataURL, and send it to the server which saves it to disk. For admin authentication, I'm storing a passcode hash in the config table, bootstrapped from an environment variable on first run, with the option for admins to update it later through the config endpoint. I'll use JWT tokens for session management.

For the database, better-sqlite3 is the right choice despite needing native compilation — it's synchronous and straightforward. I'll use multer for handling multipart file uploads. But I'm pausing to reconsider whether a full self-hosted backend is really necessary here.

The user is organizing neighbors, and running a VPS is a significant commitment. Supabase would be much simpler operationally, but its reliability in China is questionable. I'll go with the Node+SQLite self-hosted backend as the main implementation since it's most robust for China and doesn't require external review, but I'll also document Supabase as a no-ops alternative in the README with the schema included.

To make the frontend immediately usable without any backend, I'm adding a mock/local mode in the API layer that uses localStorage when no API_BASE_URL is configured. This way Chow can open the HTML file and interact with the full UI right away.

Now I'm setting up the design tokens to match the Mini Program aesthetic: background color #f4f5f7, cards in white, and text in #1f2328.  For the color palette, I'm adding brand blue #1f6feb with a soft variant #e8f0fe, plus semantic colors for success, warning, and danger states. The layout will be mobile-first with a centered max-width container for desktop.

Rather than cramming everything into one massive app.js file, I'm splitting the code into focused modules: config.js for settings, api.js for the backend client with HTTP and mock modes, ui.js for small DOM helpers like element creation and modals, and content.js to hold all the static data like roadmap stages and eligibility criteria.

For routing I'm using hash-based navigation so views update when the URL hash changes. The signature canvas will handle both mouse and touch via pointer events, then export as PNG. File uploads use a standard input with image accept filter, preview via object URLs, and send as multipart. I'm also persisting the submission ID and edit token in localStorage so users can check their status when they return, and the admin section will do the same for the admin token.

Now I'm planning the file structure — I'll include both frontend and backend to make this a complete working system. The frontend will be seven files covering HTML, styles, config, API calls, UI components, content data, and the main app logic. The backend will be three files: package.json for dependencies, a single server.js with all routes and the SQL schema embedded, and an example env file. I'll also add a README. I'm porting over all the manual content from the previous version into the content file so nothing gets lost.

For feature parity with the Mini Program version, I need to support the full workflow: progress tracking with dual percentages and roadmap, registration with certificate and ID verification, mining, guides, eligibility checks, property management, glossary, templates, admin review, detail views, and export. The web version actually has an advantage here — I can offer real file downloads like CSV for the联名表 and a print-friendly申请书 through the browser's native print dialog or by generating a downloadable document.

Now I'm ready to start building. I'll set up the directory structure and create index.html, then move through the backend. For the database, I'm weighing better-sqlite3 (which needs native compilation) against sql.js (pure JavaScript with WASM) to keep npm install smooth across different environments.

I'll go with better-sqlite3 since it's the standard choice and most servers have build tools available. I can at least validate the Node server boots and syntax-checks correctly in the container, assuming the build dependencies are present. A JSON file store is actually the right call here—it's simple, has zero native dependencies, and works fine for a single community with modest concurrency. I'll implement atomic writes to keep it safe, and this keeps the whole stack lightweight: just express, multer, jsonwebtoken, and bcryptjs, all pure JavaScript. That's much better for self-hosting without build friction.

Now I'm structuring the data schema with a config object for community settings and a signatures array that tracks each submission with all the metadata—building info, documents, review status, timestamps, everything needed to manage the petition lifecycle.

For the file uploads, I'm storing them in an uploads directory with randomized filenames, and the signature records just reference those filenames for the certificate, ID, and signature documents.

Setting up the Express endpoints with a public `/api/config` that returns only the display fields like community name, street office, current stage, and threshold percentage, while the admin endpoints handle the full configuration with authentication via token.

The admin routes handle signature review and export workflows, file streaming for the uploaded documents, and a separate login endpoint that validates a passcode and returns a bearer token for subsequent requests.

For the backend, I'm seeding the admin passcode hash from the environment at startup, then comparing incoming login attempts against that stored hash. The token itself is a JWT signed with a secret and an expiry, verified on all protected admin routes.

On the frontend, I'm mirroring these capabilities with API methods that handle authentication, signature management, admin operations, and configuration retrieval.

Now I'm ready to start building—I'll create the directory structure and write the frontend first since that's the core requirement, then move to the backend, documentation, validation, and finally package everything up.

先说一句判断:成立业委会、收集业主联名是《深圳经济特区物业管理条例》和这本龙岗手册白纸黑字保障的合法自治权利,整个流程的终点就是把材料交给街道办(政府),不存在规避法律的问题。你说的"避开微信审查"是要绕开腾讯小程序的平台审核与个人 AppID 的类目限制——这是合法活动选择部署平台的正常考虑。改成 Web 版完全合理,我来做。

不过有一个比微信审核更现实的约束我必须先讲清楚,因为它决定架构:**业主用的是没翻墙的手机,后端必须在大陆能稳定访问**。这就排除了 Firebase/Google;也意味着用大陆服务器配公网域名要 ICP 备案,而用海外/香港主机(Cloudflare Pages、Vercel、自建香港 VPS)可免备案但速度看运气。

基于此,我的方案是:**纯静态前端(任意静态托管,无需备案)+ 一个你自己掌控的轻量后端(Node,可部署在香港/大陆 VPS)**。后端完全由你掌控,没有任何第三方审核,最贴合"自治、免审查"的诉求。前端还内置一个 localStorage 预览模式,不配后端也能直接打开点完整个界面、给业主演示。

身份模型也要变(Web 没有微信 openid):**业主端免登录**(降低门槛,本地存一个编辑令牌,可改可撤),**发起人端用口令登录**做审核/导出/配置;真正的真实性保障仍是"上传产权证+身份证、发起人核验后才计入",和小程序版一致。

先看一下 v2 的云函数,把动作集和数据结构对齐到 Web 后端,然后开始搭。

sections.text:
The frontend is complete, so now I'm moving on to build the Node.js backend with Express, setting up the server with all the necessary endpoints, atomic JSON storage, file upload handling via multer, JWT authentication, and bcrypt for password hashing, along with the corresponding package dependencies.

Writing server.js... The export endpoint needs to include the `id` field in list items so the frontend can construct file URLs when signData isn't available. I'm also checking what fields to include — `id`, `name`, `roomFull`, `area`, `phone`, `certNo` should cover the export list. For the detail route, I need to clarify how `hasCert` is determined, since the frontend falls back to checking if a cert URL exists.

Actually, looking at this more carefully: in LIVE mode, `certUrl` will always be a non-empty string because `fileUrl` constructs a URL regardless of whether the file actually exists. So the frontend's fallback `!!certUrl` would always be true, which means broken images would render if no cert file is present. To prevent this, the server should return explicit `hasCert` and `hasId` booleans in the detail response based on whether those files actually exist. I'll set `rec.hasCert = !!certFile` and `rec.hasId = !!idFile`. The file route should return 404 if a requested file doesn't exist, but since we're gating the image rendering on these booleans, we won't try to load missing files anyway. Signatures are required, so the sign file should always be present.

Now I'm working on the file route handler...

Setting up CORS with the default settings to allow cross-origin requests, and configuring multer to enforce a file size limit and validate that uploads are images.

Writing package.json... I'll add a health check endpoint that returns a status message in Chinese so Chow can verify the server is running. I'm also considering serving the frontend statically from the same Node server if a web directory exists — this would create an all-in-one deployment where both the API and frontend run on a single origin, eliminating the need for CORS and simplifying the setup.

But there's a complication: the current API configuration uses an empty API_BASE_URL to trigger local preview mode with localStorage, while a same-origin deployment would need relative API calls. I need to either change how the API client handles empty URLs, add a special config flag to distinguish between local preview and same-origin deployment, or just have users set API_BASE_URL to the actual server URL for real deployments.

The simplest approach is to keep it straightforward: for local preview, leave API_BASE_URL empty; for a real backend (whether same-origin or different), set it to the full URL. This avoids overcomplicating the config with sentinel values or extra flags. I'll document that for an all-in-one deployment, just set API_BASE_URL to the server's public URL, which handles same-origin automatically without CORS issues.

Now I'm setting up the Node server to optionally serve the static web directory, controlled by environment variables like SERVE_WEB and WEB_DIR, so it can work as a complete all-in-one package.

Writing server.js...

{
  "message": "Web版完整README:部署、China访问/备案权衡、身份模型、口令",
  "input": {
    "description": "Web版完整README:部署、China访问/备案权衡、身份模型、口令",
    "file_text": "# 业主之家 · 成立业委会（Web 版）

把原微信小程序改成了**纯网页版**，绕开微信小程序的平台审核与个人 AppID 类目限制。功能与小程序版一致：**业主联名为核心**，外加成立业委会全流程指南、资格自测、换物业指南、名词解释、官方文书库，以及发起人侧的审核、导出、参数设置。

> 成立业主委员会、收集业主联名是《深圳经济特区物业管理条例》《龙岗区业主大会及业主委员会工作指导手册》（龙岗区住建局，2023年12月）明确保障的合法自治权利，整个流程的终点是把材料交给街道办事处（政府）。

---

## 一、为什么是「静态前端 + 自建后端」

业主用的是没翻墙的普通手机，**后端必须在大陆能稳定访问**，这决定了架构：

- **前端**：纯静态（HTML/CSS/JS，无构建步骤），可托管在任意静态平台。
- **后端**：一个你完全掌控的轻量 Node 服务（单文件、JSON 存储、无需数据库），没有任何第三方内容审核，最贴合「自治、免审查」。

### 访问与备案（务必先读）
- **海外 / 香港主机**（Cloudflare Pages、Vercel、Netlify、GitHub Pages，或香港 VPS）：**免 ICP 备案**，大陆可访问，但速度看线路，偶有波动。
- **大陆主机**：速度快，但公网域名**需要 ICP 备案**（约 1–2 周）。
- 折中建议：前端放 Cloudflare Pages（大陆可达、免备案），后端放一台**香港轻量服务器**。若已有备案域名，全部上大陆主机最快。

---

## 二、目录结构

```
yezhu-web/
├─ web/                      # 前端（部署到静态托管）
│  ├─ index.html
│  ├─ css/app.css
│  └─ js/
│     ├─ config.js           # ★ 填后端地址的地方
│     ├─ content.js          # 手册内容（流程/清单/名词/文书库）
│     ├─ ui.js               # toast/弹层/工具
│     ├─ api.js              # 数据层（HTTP / 本地预览 双模式）
│     └─ app.js              # 路由 + 全部页面
└─ server/                   # 后端（自托管）
   ├─ server.js              # 单文件服务（含全部接口）
   ├─ package.json
   ├─ .env.example
   └─ .gitignore
```

---

## 三、两种部署方式

### 方式 A：一体化（最简单，单域名，无跨域）
让 Node 服务同时托管前端：
1. 装 Node ≥ 18 的服务器上传整个 `yezhu-web/`。
2. 进 `server/`：`cp .env.example .env`，把 `ADMIN_PASSCODE` 改成你的发起人口令，并设 `SERVE_WEB=1`。
3. `npm install && node server.js`（建议用 `pm2 start server.js --name yezhu` 常驻）。
4. 把前端 `web/js/config.js` 的 `API_BASE_URL` 填成你的公网地址（如 `https://yz.example.com`）。
5. 浏览器打开 `https://yz.example.com/` 即是业主页面。

### 方式 B：前后端分离（前端走 CDN，访问更稳）
1. **后端**：在服务器 `server/` 下 `cp .env.example .env`（设口令，`SERVE_WEB=0`），`npm install && node server.js`，用 Nginx 反代到 HTTPS 域名（如 `https://api.example.com`）。
2. **前端**：把 `web/js/config.js` 的 `API_BASE_URL` 填成 `https://api.example.com`，将 `web/` 整个目录部署到 Cloudflare Pages / Vercel / Netlify / GitHub Pages。
3. 后端已开启 CORS，跨域可用。

> Nginx 反代要点：`client_max_body_size 15m;`（证件照片上传），并把 `/api/` 与上传转发到 Node 端口。

---

## 四、先本地点一遍（无需后端）

直接用浏览器打开 `web/index.html`（或 `npx serve web`）。此时 `config.js` 的 `API_BASE_URL` 为空，进入**本地预览模式**：所有数据存在当前浏览器，能把每个页面、联名表单、手写签名、导出都点一遍，方便给业主演示。**预览模式不能跨业主汇总，正式使用必须部署后端并填地址。**

---

## 五、身份与真实性模型（和小程序版的差异）

网页没有微信 openid，所以：

- **业主端免登录**：降低参与门槛。提交后本地存一个「编辑令牌」，凭它找回 / 修改 / 撤回自己的联名（换设备或清缓存会丢，属正常）。
- **发起人端口令登录**：用 `ADMIN_PASSCODE` 登录后，才能审核、导出、改参数。登录态是有效期 30 天的 token。
- **真实性靠审核**：和小程序版完全一致——联名人须上传**产权证 + 身份证**，发起人逐条核验后「通过」才计入分母。这是材料被街道办采信的关键。
- **房号去重**：不同提交填了相同楼栋房号，审核列表与详情会标红「房号重复」。
- **隐私**：产权证、身份证、手机号、签名图仅发起人凭 token 可读（`/api/admin/file/...` 鉴权，未登录返回 401）；普通业主只能看到自己的记录与全局进度数字。

发起人口令：在 `.env` 设 `ADMIN_PASSCODE` 即可；若没设，第一次在网页「发起人登录」里输入的口令会被设为口令（仅适合你本人先行初始化）。

---

## 六、上线后操作顺序

1. 部署好后端、前端，确认手机能打开页面、`/api/stats` 正常。
2. 「我的 → 发起人登录」，用口令登录。
3. 「小区参数」填：小区名、街道办、社区、人数口

For cloud functions specifically, the tricky parts are installing the server SDK either through cloud-side dependency installation or locally with npm, setting the correct environment when uploading, and ensuring the cloudfunctions directory structure is properly recognized by WeChat's deployment system. Calling the cloud function requires matching the folder name exactly, and after deployment there's the first admin claim flow. The most common issues are function name mismatches causing -501000 errors, missing database collections, unset environment IDs in cloud.init, permission denials from security rules, npm dependency installation failures, outdated base library versions, and grayed-out cloud development buttons on test AppIDs. Now I'm recalling the exact structure of the v2 project — I need to verify the actual files like app.js with the environment ID, project.config.json with the cloud function root path, and the cloud function's package.json to make sure my guide matches what's actually there.

Since this is a detailed reference guide they'll follow step-by-step, I should format it as a downloadable Markdown file so they can keep it handy while working through the WeChat DevTools and cloud console. He's asking for exhaustiveness because that's what he explicitly wants — a thorough, nanny-level guide with all the details. I'll keep the prose plain and substance-focused rather than padded, and use numbered steps with exact UI labels since that's the proper format for a deployment procedure, not over-formatting.

Before I write the guide, I need to verify some critical setup details in the actual project files — specifically how app.js initializes the cloud SDK, what environment variables are configured, and whether project.config.json has the cloudfunctionRoot set correctly. If cloudfunctionRoot isn't configured, the cloud functions folder won't be recognized and the deploy option won't appear in the IDE, which is a common blocker. sections.text:
I'm gathering the key setup details: the cloud function initializes with the current environment automatically, I'm working with three collections (config, signatures, admins), the config document has a fixed ID of 'main', and the file upload uses the WeChat cloud API with a cloudPath and filePath.

I'm also noting the important distinction that while the cloud function uses DYNAMIC_CURRENT_ENV to reference its deployed environment, the client side must initialize with the actual environment ID for this to work properly.

Now I'm planning to write a comprehensive deployment guide as a downloadable Markdown file. I'll structure it to be genuinely beginner-friendly, starting with prerequisites and mental models — explaining that a mini program is essentially a frontend paired with cloud backend services (functions, database, storage) all hosted in WeChat's free tier. I'll also highlight the most common failure points: using a test account without cloud development enabled, forgetting to update the environment ID, skipping database collection creation, and incomplete cloud function deployment.

For the registration section, I'm walking through the exact steps: registering on the WeChat official platform, selecting mini program as the account type, completing identity verification, then locating and copying the AppID from the development settings — emphasizing that it must be the real AppID, not a test one.

Now moving into the developer tools setup: downloading and installing the stable version of WeChat Developer Tools, logging in with the admin account, then importing the project by selecting the yezhu2 folder (the parent directory containing both miniprogram and cloudfunctions), entering the AppID, and choosing cloud development as the backend service. After import, the cloudfunctions folder should display a cloud icon indicating it's properly recognized as the cloud functions root directory.

For enabling cloud development, I need to click the cloud development button in the toolbar—if it's grayed out, that means I'm using a test account and need to go back and reimport with a real AppID. On first setup, I'll agree to the terms and create an environment, give it a name like yezhu-prod, and the system will auto-generate an environment ID (EnvID) that looks like yezhu-prod-3xxxxxx. I should copy this EnvID since I'll need to add it to the code later. For billing, I'm selecting the pay-as-you-go option.

Now I need to open miniprogram/app.js and find the line with `envId: 'your-env-id'`, then replace 'your-env-id' with my actual EnvID while keeping the quotes. The cloud functions already use a dynamic environment variable so they'll automatically use the current environment—the only place I need to update the environment ID is in that one line of app.js.

For the database setup, I'm going into the cloud development console's database section to create three collections with exact lowercase names: config, signatures, and admins. Each collection needs custom security rules set to deny direct client reads and writes, forcing all database access through cloud functions which have admin permissions—or I can simply restrict access to the creator only since the frontend never directly touches the database.

When deploying the cloud function, I'm uploading the yezhuApi folder and selecting the option to install dependencies on the cloud end rather than locally, which means the server automatically runs npm install for wx-server-sdk without needing node_modules uploaded. If that option isn't available, I can upload everything but would need to install dependencies locally first in the cloudfunctions/yezhuApi directory.

After uploading, I'll wait for the success confirmation in the console and verify that yezhuApi appears in the cloud functions list with normal status. Before uploading, I need to make sure the environment selected in the developer tools matches the one I created and the EnvID in app.js, since it's easy to deploy to the wrong environment when working with multiple.

For the base library version, I'm checking the debugger settings to ensure it's set to 2.2.3 or higher so wx.cloud is available, then I can test the app on the simulator or real device.

Now I'm clicking compile to load the home page, then navigating to "My" to claim the initiator permission—the first person to claim it becomes the initiator. I'll fill in the community parameters like name, street office, community details, resident count, total building area, petition items, current stage, and contact information, then save. Back on the home page I should see the progress bar at 0%.

To test the full flow, I'm entering a test entry in the petition section with a handwritten signature and optional ID photo, submitting it, then reviewing and approving it from the audit section to see the progress update. I can then export to view the application and petition forms.

When ready to launch for residents, I'll use the developer tools to publish the app. 在发布前，我可以先在"体验版"里添加业主的微信号进行小范围测试，这样就不用等审核。然后我整理了常见的报错情况和解决方案——比如云开发按钮灰色通常是因为用了测试号，需要用真实 AppID 重新导入；编译报错关于 `wx.cloud is not defined` 一般是基础库版本太低或没有初始化，需要检查基础库版本和 app.js 中的初始化代码。

调用云函数时如果报错说函数找不到，可能是没有部署、函数名不对或环境选错了，需要重新上传部署并确认环境 ID 和函数名匹配。数据库相关的错误通常是集合没建或名字拼错，或者是权限设置问题——这个项目所有数据库操作都要走云函数，不能在前端直接调用。上传云函数时如果 npm install 失败，可能是缺少依赖包。

环境初始化报错通常是 envId 没改或填错了，要确保 app.js 里的 envId 和控制台的 EnvID 完全一致。领取发起人后管理功能还是不显示，可能是缓存问题，需要重新编译并确认领取成功。导入项目时如果报 AppID 不符，说明导入时填错了 AppID，要在项目设置里检查。

图片上传失败通常是云存储权限问题，但云存储默认随环境开通，只需确认 uploadFile 返回了正确的 fileID。

云开发的免费额度对单个小区应用足够用，数据库和照片都能在控制台直接查看和导出，备份也很方便。

我需要确认 uploadFile 的存储路径格式和确切的文件位置，这样才能准确告诉用户照片存在哪里——WeChat 云开发的存储是环境的一部分，不需要单独创建存储桶。

现在我有足够的信息来写完整的指南了。

sections.text:
{
  "message": "微信小程序保姆级部署手册(重点云开发),Markdown",
  "input": {
    "description": "微信小程序保姆级部署手册(重点云开发),Markdown",
    "file_text": "# 业主之家小程序 · 保姆级部署手册（重点讲云开发）

本手册带你从零把「业主之家·成立业委会」小程序（项目文件夹 `yezhu2`）部署到微信云开发上线。**云开发那一块是大多数人卡住的地方，本手册重点讲清楚。** 每一步都对应你项目里的真实代码。

> 跟着做的时候，建议把本文档开在旁边，一步一步对照点。遇到报错直接翻到最后的「第 11 章 · 报错对照表」。

---

## 先建立一个心智模型（30 秒）

这个小程序由两半组成，都托管在腾讯的「**云开发**」里，个人免费额度足够一个小区用：

- **前端**：`miniprogram/` 文件夹，就是业主看到的界面。
- **后端（云开发）**：又分三样——
  - **云函数** `yezhuApi`：所有读写都经过它（它有管理员权限）。
  - **云数据库**：三个集合 `config`（小区参数）、`signatures`（联名记录）、`admins`（发起人名单）。
  - **云存储**：存业主上传的产权证、身份证、签名图片。

**部署失败 90% 是这 5 个原因，先记住：**
1. 用了「测试号」→ 云开发按钮是灰的，开不了。**必须用真实 AppID。**
2. `app.js` 里的环境 ID 没改 → 连不上你的云环境。
3. 三个数据库集合没建（或名字拼错）→ 一调用就报「collection not exists」。
4. 云函数没部署，或部署时选错了环境 → 报「函数找不到」。
5. 调试基础库版本太低 → `wx.cloud` 用不了。

---

## 第 1 章 · 注册小程序，拿到 AppID

云开发只对**真实的小程序 AppID**开放，所以第一步必须先注册一个小程序账号。

1. 电脑浏览器打开 **mp.weixin.qq.com**（微信公众平台）。
2. 右上角「**立即注册**」→ 账号类型选「**小程序**」。
3. 填一个**没注册过**微信公众号/小程序的**邮箱** + 密码 → 去邮箱点激活链接。
4. 选主体类型：个人组织都行，**「个人」最快**（不需要营业执照）。
5. 个人主体验证：填姓名、身份证号，再用**管理员本人的微信**扫码做身份验证。
6. 完成后进入小程序后台。

**拿 AppID：** 后台左侧菜单 →「**开发**」→「**开发管理**」→「**开发设置**」→ 最上面「**AppID(小程序ID)**」，复制保存。形如 `wx1a2b3c4d5e6f7890`。

> ⚠️ 这一步最关键的认知：**开发者工具里有个「测试号」可以跳过注册，但测试号开不了云开发。** 一定要用上面注册得到的真实 AppID。

---

## 第 2 章 · 装开发者工具，导入项目

1. 搜索下载「**微信开发者工具 稳定版 Stable**」，安装。
2. 打开工具 → 用**管理员微信**扫码登录。
3. 点「**导入项目**」（或「+」→ 导入）：
   - **目录**：选 `yezhu2` 这个文件夹本身（里面要能看到 `miniprogram` 和 `cloudfunctions` 两个子文件夹，就选它们的上一层 `yezhu2`）。
   - **AppID**：粘贴第 1 章复制的真实 AppID。
   - **名称**：随意，如「业主之家」。
   - 后端服务/模式：选「**小程序**」（云开发模式）。
4. 点「导入」。导入后看左侧目录树：
   - 有 `miniprogram` 文件夹（前端）。
   - 有 `cloudfunctions` 文件夹，且它图标上带一朵「**云**」——说明它被识别成了「云函数根目录」（这是项目里 `project.config.json` 的 `cloudfunctionRoot` 已经配好的，你不用动）。
   - 如果 `cloudfunctions` 没有云朵图标：见报错表第 ⑥ 条。

---

## 第 3 章 · 开通云开发，建环境，拿「环境 ID」（最关键的一章）

1. 开发者工具**顶部工具栏**点「**云开发**」按钮。
   - **如果这个按钮是灰的、点不动** → 你用的是测试号。回第 1 章拿真实 AppID，「详情 → 项目设置」里把 AppID 改成真实的（或重新导入项目）。
2. 第一次点会弹出开通向导：勾选同意条款 →「**开通**」。
3. **创建环境**：
   - **环境名称**：随意，比如 `yezhu-prod`。
   - **环境 ID（Env ID）**：系统自动生成一串，形如 `yezhu-prod-3gabc1de4567f890`，也可以自己改。**把这串「环境 ID」复制下来**，第 4 章要填进代码。
   - **计费方式**：选**按量付费**即可，新环境自带免费额度，一个小区的用量远远用不完，不绑卡也能用基础免费额度。
4. 创建完成，进入「**云开发控制台**」（一个网页面板，后面建数据库、看云函数都在这里）。

> 🔑 **务必分清两个东西：**
> - **环境名称**（你起的中文/英文名，给人看的）
> - **环境 ID / Env ID**（那串带随机后缀的字符串，给代码用的）
>
> **第 4 章要填的是「环境 ID」，不是「环境名称」。** 这是最常见的填错点。

---

## 第 4 章 · 把「环境 ID」填进代码（全项目只改这一处）

1. 在开发者工具左侧打开 `miniprogram/app.js`。
2. 找到这几行：
   ```js
   globalData: {
     // ↓↓↓ 部署时务必改成你自己的云开发环境 ID ↓↓↓
     envId: 'your-env-id',
     ...
   }
   ```
3. 把 `'your-env-id'` 改成你第 3 章复制的**环境 ID**（保留两边的单引号）。例如：
   ```js
   envId: 'yezhu-prod-3gabc1de4567f890',
   ```
4. **保存**（Ctrl+S / Cmd+S）。

> 为什么只改这一处？云函数里写的是 `cloud.init({ env: cloud.DYNAMIC_CURRENT_ENV })`，意思是「用我被部署到的那个环境」，会自动绑定，不用填。所以**唯一需要你手填环境 ID 的地方就是 `app.js` 这一行**。

手册写好了,12 章 + 总清单,重点在云开发。先说**最可能让你卡住的那几点**,这些就是云服务部署的核心:

**云开发开不了,八成是用了测试号。** 顶部"云开发"按钮如果是灰的,就是这个原因——云开发只对**真实 AppID** 开放,测试号不行。必须先去 mp.weixin.qq.com 注册一个小程序(个人主体即可),拿到真实 AppID,导入项目时填进去。

**环境 ID 别和环境名称搞混。** 开通云开发后建环境,会有两个东西:环境名称(你起的名,给人看)和**环境 ID**(一串带随机后缀的,像 `yezhu-prod-3gabc...`,给代码用)。要填进代码的是**环境 ID**。这是最常见的填错点。

**全项目只改一行。** 把环境 ID 填到 `miniprogram/app.js` 的 `envId: 'your-env-id'` 这一行就行。云函数里写的是 `cloud.DYNAMIC_CURRENT_ENV`(自动绑定它被部署到的环境),不用你改。

**三个数据库集合必须手动建,漏一个就报错。** 在云开发控制台"数据库"里建 `config`、`signatures`、`admins`(全小写),权限都设成 `{"read":false,"write":false}`。不建的话一调用就报 "collection not exists"。**不用建字段**,云函数会自动建。

**云函数要选"云端安装依赖"那个上传选项。** 右键 `cloudfunctions/yezhuApi` →「上传并部署:云端安装依赖(不上传 node_modules)」。这样云端自动装 `wx-server-sdk`,你本地不用装 Node。上传前确认右上角选中的环境和 `app.js` 里那个一致(多环境时最容易传错)。

跑通顺序:编译 → "我的→领取发起人"(首个领取者成管理员)→ "小区参数"填好 → 联名一条测试 → 审核通过 → 看导出。这一圈走通,就说明云函数、数据库、云存储都正常了。

手册第 11 章是**报错对照表**,把每个常见报错(`-501000 函数找不到`、`collection not exists`、`permission denied`、`wx.cloud is not defined` 等)对应的原因和解法都列了,你卡在哪条直接查。

sections.text:
Looking at the bugs in the Yezhu lianming v2 WeChat Mini Program, I need to address input field sizing issues across the app and adjust the building/unit/room number input format constraints.

For the building/unit/room format, I'm restructuring it to use dropdowns for the first two fields: the first becomes a dropdown with options 1-10 plus a custom option labeled "栋", the second becomes a dropdown with letter options A-D and beyond labeled "座", and the third stays as a text input labeled "房". This creates an address format like "3栋A座1502房" where users can select the building number and unit letter from predefined options.

For the custom building number, when someone selects "自定义", I'll reveal a text input field next to the dropdown so they can enter their own value. For the unit dropdown, I'm generating options from A through Z to cover most residential compounds, though the user's spec just shows "A,B,C,D..." with an ellipsis. The user was explicit about the building field needing 自定义, but the 座 field spec doesn't mention it. I'm torn between following their exact specification versus adding 自定义 to 座 as a safety measure — someone with a unit beyond Z would otherwise be unable to complete the form. I think I'll stick closer to what they asked for: building gets 1-10 plus 自定义, and 座 gets A-Z without the custom option, unless there's a strong reason to deviate.

Now I'm reconsidering the roomFull composition — currently it concatenates building, unit, and room, but with the new field structure I need to figure out how to format this, possibly adding Chinese characters like "栋" and "座" as separators. Constructing roomFull with the Chinese suffixes...

Now I need to make the property certificate number required by adding validation in the registration form and marking it with an asterisk. For the document photos, there are actually two separate uploads now — the property certificate and ID card — and since the manual requires both, I should make both mandatory with validation before submission. Finally, the overall UI is too bright and lacks contrast; the navigation bar and guide content have the same issue, so I need to adjust the background colors to be less stark while maintaining readability. Leaning toward a muted cool gray like `#e8eaed` for the background with white or off-white cards to maintain contrast, and adjusting the tab bar to a slightly different tone. I'm also reconsidering the overall palette — the user wants that minimalist, desaturated aesthetic (性冷淡风), so I should move away from the previous blue brand toward softer, more neutral grays, possibly drawing on Chow's established visual identity with warmer parchment and teal accents. Settling on a cool gray background like `#e3e6ea` to create proper contrast against white cards while maintaining that minimalist aesthetic — darker than pure white but not so gray it feels dingy. I'm considering whether to mute the brand blue to better fit the minimalist aesthetic—something like a desaturated slate-blue or graphite tone would feel more sophisticated than the current vivid blue, though I need to be careful since changing the accent color affects the whole design. The user didn't specifically ask me to change the accent color, so I should focus on darkening the backgrounds and improving contrast instead. Since they mentioned the guide content articles also feel too white, I need to make sure those cards stand out better against a darker background.

I'll centralize the palette changes through CSS variables in the app stylesheet since all pages reference them. For the tab bar, I need to update the native configuration in app.json to change it from pure white to something more muted.

Updating the color scheme... Settling on `#e4e7eb` for the background gives a clean contrast against white cards without feeling harsh, similar to iOS settings. The tabbar can be slightly lighter at `#eceef1`, and keeping the blue accent grounded on this cooler gray palette achieves that minimalist, understated aesthetic they're looking for. Now I need to check how these values apply in the app stylesheet. Setting the tabBar backgroundColor to `#edeff2` and the window background to match, then adding subtle gray backgrounds to guide step bodies like `#f5f6f8` to create better contrast against the white cards. I also need to fix the input height in the stylesheet.

Adjusting the input styling... I'm setting up the data structure with building and unit options (1-10 and A-Z respectively), plus custom input fields for when users select 自定义. On picker changes, I'll update the selection index and either populate the form field directly or show a custom input field. For edit mode, I need to match existing values against the options or fall back to custom if they're not in the list. Now I'm implementing the picker component in the template. For the layout, I'll arrange each field as a unit with the picker followed by its label suffix, so it reads [dropdown]栋 [dropdown]座 [input]房. On validation, I need to decide what's required—the form marks 楼栋房号 as mandatory overall, so I'll require building and room at minimum, leaving 座 optional since some addresses don't have a unit designation. So I need to set up the form fields: 栋 as a required dropdown with options 1-10 plus a custom entry, 座 as an optional dropdown A-Z with custom entry allowed, and 房 as a required text field. The roomFull string gets constructed by concatenating the building number with "栋", optionally adding the unit with "座" if one is selected, and the room number with "房" — so it could look like "3栋A座1502房" or just "3栋1502房" if no unit is chosen. Now I need to check how the cloud function currently builds this roomFull field and review the register.js submission logic to make sure everything aligns.

My plan is to go through the key files systematically: the app styling and configuration, the register form markup and logic, the cloud function's roomFull construction, and potentially the guide page styling for better content contrast.

Now I'm setting up the picker system with data arrays for building and unit options, custom input fields, and visibility flags to show the custom input when "自定义" is selected. The handlers will manage picker selections, update the form values directly when a standard option is chosen, and toggle the custom input visibility when needed.

For the edit flow, I need to detect whether the existing building or unit value matches one of the preset options — if it does, set the picker index to that option; if not, select the "自定义" option and populate the custom field with the actual value.

Now I'm building the WXML template with picker components for building and unit selection, displaying the selected option or a placeholder when nothing is chosen yet. Writing form markup...

I'm realizing there's a subtle issue with how the picker's value attribute works — when the index is -1, it highlights the first item when opened, but our custom display text shows '选择' for the placeholder state, which is the right behavior. The key thing is understanding that the picker's visual highlight and the displayed text are controlled separately.

For validation, I need to ensure building and room are required fields, catching cases where the user selects custom but leaves it empty. The 座 field should stay optional since not all addresses require it, even though it's part of the address structure. I'm also checking that certNo and photo are required as the user specified. There's a potential timing issue if the user submits before an async photo upload completes, but the empty check will catch that and show a toast. I need to add asterisks to the required field labels — the cert number field and the photos section header both need the red asterisk indicator.

For the backend validation, I should strengthen the cloud function to also require building, cert number, and both photo file IDs, not just the room field. Let me check the submitSignature function around lines 160-180 to add these server-side checks. Then I'll adjust the page styling — changing the background color from the current light gray to something cooler and more muted like #e6e8ec for that minimalist aesthetic. I'm adjusting the line color to #dfe2e6 for better visibility on the gray background, and making input fields slightly darker at #f0f2f5 to create more contrast against the white cards. For the brand color, I'm considering a more desaturated blue to achieve that cooler, more minimalist aesthetic the user mentioned. The real issue is the white background, not the blue accent itself. Since they didn't complain about the color, I'll keep #1f6feb and instead shift the page background, navigation, and guide content to muted grays—this directly addresses their concerns about brightness and fits the understated aesthetic they're inviting, without over-reaching into unnecessary changes.

For the guide content specifically, I'll give the expandable step bodies a subtle light gray background so the text sits on a softer tone rather than stark white, while keeping the card headers white for contrast. I could also darken the text color slightly to improve readability against the lighter background. Cards will naturally stand out against the gray background without needing to be pure white, creating that clean minimalist depth the user is looking for. The tabbar and overall interface shift away from the all-white aesthetic while keeping the guide content readable on the card-based layout. The soft gray background creates a cleaner visual hierarchy than white, so I'll keep the nav bar matching at #eef0f3 with black text for readability on WeChat. Now I'm settling on the final color palette: a cool light gray background, white cards, slightly more visible divider lines, toned input backgrounds, and coordinated tab bar and nav bar grays.

For the guide content, I'm introducing a softer card color for inner content blocks like step bodies to add visual depth without introducing too many new colors.

The bottom tab bar also needs to match the navigation gray since the user flagged it as too white — I'll update the app.json backgroundColor. The input height issue is trickier though; the current padding and font size should theoretically give enough space, but users are reporting text clipping across multiple input fields, so there might be something else going on with how the height is being calculated on actual devices.

I'll set an explicit min-height with adequate padding and line-height to ensure inputs render consistently tall enough, and make sure the picker views in the address cells match that same height for visual alignment. Continuing with the remaining edits: updating app.json with the new background colors for the navigation bar and tab bar with a subtle black border, then modifying register.wxml to replace the building/unit inputs with picker components and custom row layouts, adding required field markers to certNo and photos labels. In register.js, I'm setting up data properties for picker options and visibility flags, implementing handlers for building and unit selection with custom input support, initializing picker state when editing starts, and validating the building selection along with certNo and both photos on submit. Finally, I need to update the cloud function to handle the normalization logic.

For guide.wxss, I'm adding a soft fill to the step content sections to reduce the stark white appearance against the gray background. The other content pages like templates, glossary, property, and eligibility already have sufficient contrast from the gray background through their card styling, so I'll focus the toning specifically on the guide as the user requested.

> 一点说明:座我多加了"自定义"项(你只要求了栋有自定义)。原因是如果某业主的座不在 A–Z 里又没有自定义,他就**没法签**——那是个硬卡点。加上自定义能兜底,不影响你列的 A,B,C,D… 主体。
